processing: Leaf from the Longjing area is taken down the black tea path of withering, rolling, oxidation and drying rather than pan-firing as a green tea. No standard for this name is documented.
harvest_season: Not fixed by any standard; Hangzhou black teas are usually made from spring leaf.
appearance_dry: Dark, thin twisted leaf, as is usual for Hangzhou black tea.
appearance_liquor: Clear reddish amber, as with other Zhejiang black teas.
appearance_wet: Small, soft coppery leaves, typical of tender-picked Chinese black tea.
taste_profile: Little is documented for this name; Zhejiang black teas are generally gentle, with a soft sweetness and little astringency.

brewing.notes: Handle it as a delicate Chinese black: water a little off the boil and short steeps.

vintage_note: There is no established way this name is sold. Treat it as a current or recent spring-harvest black tea, as is usual for the class, and ask which harvest and which area it comes from.
description:
Longjing Hong Cha means simply 'Longjing black tea': black tea made in the Hangzhou area where Long Jing green tea grows. It is a trade description more than a defined tea with its own standard.

The method is that of black tea rather than the pan-firing that makes Long Jing what it is, so nothing of the flat green leaf or its chestnut aroma should be expected.

The established black tea of this district is Jiu Qu Hong Mei, from Shuangpu in Hangzhou's Xihu district, and it uses old Longjing population bushes. Some goods sold under the Longjing black name may be close to it, so that tea is a useful reference point when tasting.

When buying, ask where the leaf grew and who made it. 'Longjing' on a black tea does not guarantee origin inside the protected West Lake area.
history: Little is documented about where and when black tea under this name was first made, or who made it known. A 2012 report said Hangzhou was preparing a certification mark and production standard for West Lake Longjing black tea; what came of that is unclear. It should be read as a modern descriptive name, unless a maker can show otherwise.
